artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Σ be a finite alphabet and let Σ* denote the free monoid of all finite words over Σ. A word u is a factor of a word v if v = xuy for some x, y ∈ Σ*. Let p be a pattern, i.e. a word over an alphabet of variables. A word w ∈ Σ* is said to encounter p if there exists a non-erasing morphism h from the variable alphabet of p to Σ* such that h(p) is a factor of w; otherwise w is p-free. A p-free word w ∈ Σ* is called maximal p-free if for every letter a ∈ Σ, both aw and wa encounter p (equivalently, w cannot be extended on either side while remaining p-free).

Prove or disprove the following statement: for every alphabet Σ, every pattern p, and every p-free word w ∈ Σ*, there exists a maximal p-free word M ∈ Σ* such that w is a factor of M.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turned up the WORDS conferences problem compilations and related work on extendability of pattern-free words (e.g., Petrova–Shur on binary cube-free words admitting only finite extensions), but no source confirming a proof or disproof of this specific conjecture about every p-free word being a factor of some maximal p-free word for general patterns p. Status appears unresolved in the literature accessible via search.
